explanation: Sources vary on how strongly it registers, but there is general agreement that jabbing an index finger at a specific person reads as accusatory or rude in Germany, similar to broader European norms; using an open hand to indicate someone is the safer choice. Pointing at objects or directions with the index finger is generally unremarkable.
local_tip: When indicating a specific person, gesture with an open hand rather than a single pointed finger.

also_check.note: Pointing with the index finger at a person is considered very impolite; an open hand or slight bow is used instead.
Pointing at people is common and rarely called out, but it's still seen as a bit brusque or impolite in more formal settings.
Pointing with the index finger is considered offensive; people point with the thumb or an open hand instead.
